---
title: "Dependencies"
---

In order to use VSCode effectively, there are some additional programs or applications that we also recommend you install or use on your own.

* GitHub:
  * We recommend using GitHub. If you do not already have a GitHub account, we recommend following the [instructions from GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
* Copilot:
  * Copilot is now built into VS Code, so it will appear whether or not you intend to use it. Our recommended profile also lists the separate GitHub Copilot and Copilot Chat extensions, which VS Code no longer needs. To use Copilot you need a GitHub account: there is a free plan, verified students can get the Copilot Student plan at no cost through [GitHub Education](https://github.com/education), and verified teachers may be eligible for free access to Copilot Pro.
  * [GitHub's setup instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/quickstart) cover signing in. If you would rather not use Copilot at all, turn on the `chat.disableAIFeatures` setting, which [hides and disables the AI features](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/setup#_remove-ai-features-from-vs-code), and nothing else in this guide changes.
* Skim:
  * Skim is a PDF viewer, which you can [download from the internet](https://skim-app.sourceforge.io/). We recommend setting this as your default PDF viewer.
  * Once Skim is open, go to the top toolbar menu. Select Skim > Settings.
  * In the settings pane that opens, click Sync on the top right.
  * Check off the boxes for "Check for file changes" and "Reload automatically"
  * In the PDF-TeX Sync support section, set the "Preset" to Visual Studio Code
* MacTeX:
  * MacTeX is the standard TeX distribution on macOS, which you can [download from the internet](https://tug.org/mactex/).
  * If you already have a TeX distribution installed on your computer, you do not need to install MacTeX as well.
* Pandoc:
  * Pandoc allows you to knit `.Rmd` files to PDF files. You can [install the latest release from the internet](https://pandoc.org/installing.html).
